title: An incidence rate with an exact Poisson interval
summary: Events per person-year of follow-up in a cohort, with the exact (Garwood) Poisson 95% interval.

sizing._why: The catalog has no precision form for a single rate. Sizing one needs the expected number of events for a target interval width, which is a calculation the app does not offer; borrowing the proportion-precision form would size a different quantity.

pinned_defaults: R: T = person_years. poisson.test defaults to T = 1 and silently returns the interval for the event COUNT, not the rate.
Python: method='exact-c', the central exact (Garwood) interval R reports. confint_poisson offers about a dozen methods.
Python: the exposure argument is the person-time; at 1 it gives the interval for the count.
_poisson_assumption: The exact interval assumes events are Poisson: independent, at one rate for everyone. When some people have repeated events the data are overdispersed and this interval is too narrow; use a negative binomial or a robust (sandwich) interval from a rate regression instead.
